output.headline: Adds $59,460 to Noll & Tam's design work for moving portables at Urban Promise Academy
output.summary: This amendment adds $59,460, including a $5,400 contingency, to the architecture contract with Noll & Tam Architects. The firm will review existing documents, draw base plans, visit the site and meet with district staff about the Urban Promise Academy portable relocation project. The contract limit rises from $31,988 to $91,448, and the end date moves from December 31, 2023 to December 31, 2024.

output.headline: Approves a contract with AMN Allied Services for up to $100,000 in special education services
output.summary: AMN Allied Services will provide special education services that students' Individualized Education Programs require. This is a master contract with a nonpublic, nonsectarian school or agency, meaning a private provider outside the district's own schools. It runs July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $99,000 for Sown To Grow's social-emotional learning screening software
output.summary: Sown To Grow, Inc. will provide web-based software that screens students for social-emotional learning needs at all interested schools. The Community Schools and Student Services Department manages it for August 1, 2022 through June 29, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $15,400 and more time for a therapist serving students and families at Chabot Elementary
output.summary: This amendment adds $15,400 to a contract for a therapist who works with the principal and school psychologist to support students and families at Chabot Elementary School. The contract limit rises from $6,250 to $21,650, and the end date moves from November 10, 2022 to June 15, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, this change.

output.headline: Approves two tentative agreements with SEIU Local 1021 on safety training and a connectivity pilot
output.summary: The board is approving two tentative agreements (called memoranda of understanding) with the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), Local 1021. One covers safety training and the other covers the City of Oakland Affordable Connectivity Plan Pilot. Approval is pending compliance with state disclosure rules and any follow-up required by the Alameda County Office of Education. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $21,250 for East Bay Consortium's college advising at Castlemont High
output.summary: East Bay Consortium will give Castlemont High School students senior transcript reviews, one-on-one advising, college information sessions, financial aid help and workshops on transferring from community college to a four-year school. The service period is January 4 through May 31, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $27,000 for East Bay Consortium's post-high-school advising at Madison Park Academy
output.summary: East Bay Consortium advisors will meet with all seniors at Madison Park Academy-Upper twice a year, in fall and spring, to help them prepare for life after high school. The service period is October 10, 2022 through May 26, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $12,500 for Bay Area Community Resources' gang intervention at Castlemont High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will hold one-on-one and group intervention sessions about gang involvement for identified students at Castlemont High School. The service period is January 4 through May 31, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies $3,575 for LifeSaver CPR to train 65 district staff in CPR, defibrillator use and first aid
output.summary: LifeSaver CPR provided a one-day, on-site training on cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and first aid for 65 district staff on August 5, 2022. The Community Schools and Student Services Department arranged it. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement for a training date that has already passed.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $7,000 for Growing Together to support garden and food field trips
output.summary: Growing Together - Bay Area will help run environment, food and garden education field trips by prepping food, setting up the produce bar, serving lunch to students on the trips, and cleaning up. The service period is January 10 through May 31, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Hires Atlas Technical Consultants for up to $24,446.40 of engineering on three schools' solar projects
output.summary: Atlas Technical Consultants would provide geotechnical engineering, testing and plan review during construction of the Solar Initiative projects at Acorn Woodland Elementary, Lockwood STEAM Academy and New Highland Academy. The limit is $24,446.40, which includes up to $2,222.40 for additional services. Work is scheduled from February 9, 2023 to August 31, 2023, and is paid from the Measure Y bond fund.

output.headline: Hires Consolidated Engineering Laboratories for up to $50,258.78 of testing on three schools' solar projects
output.summary: Consolidated Engineering Laboratories would provide materials testing and special construction inspection, as required by the Division of the State Architect, for the Solar Initiative projects at Acorn Woodland Elementary, Lockwood STEAM Academy and New Highland Academy. The limit is $50,258.78, which includes up to $4,568.98 for additional services. Work is scheduled from February 9, 2023 to August 31, 2023, and is paid from the Measure Y bond fund.

output.headline: Hires KDI Group for up to $46,800 of construction inspection on three schools' solar projects
output.summary: KDI Group, Inc. would serve as the inspector of record for the Solar Initiative construction projects at Acorn Woodland Elementary, Lockwood STEAM Academy and New Highland Academy. The limit is $46,800, which includes up to $3,800 for additional services. Work is scheduled from February 9, 2023 to August 31, 2023, and is paid from the Measure Y bond fund.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $65,000 for a consultant to support Oakland Athletic League middle school sports
output.summary: B Gammage, The Creative Consultant, will provide administrative support for middle school sports programs run through the Oakland Athletic League. The service period is December 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $16,000 for J. Chacón Consulting to coach three high school principals
output.summary: J. Chacón Consulting, LLC will coach three high school principals twice a month for six months, hold monthly alignment meetings with the High School Network Superintendent, and make site visits as requested. The service period is January 3 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,000 for Axis Mundi to provide therapists at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: Axis Mundi Center for Mental Health will provide therapists who work with Hoover Elementary School students one-on-one and in groups on managing emotions and building healthy relationships, six hours a week. They will also consult with and train school staff. The service period is August 8, 2022 through May 26, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

vendor.name: Axis Mundi Center for Mental Health

output.headline: Ratifies up to $30,821.50 for High Expectations' family engagement work at Bella Vista Elementary
output.summary: High Expectations will run two-day Family Engagement Learning Institutes and coach staff and Family Engagement Teams at Bella Vista Elementary School. The goal is to raise student achievement and improve school climate. The service period is January 9 through May 26, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $45,000 for a contractor to support teacher recruitment and events
output.summary: An individual contractor will support teacher recruitment and organize and plan recruitment events for the Academics and Instruction Department. The service period is November 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $276,300 for Saving Shorty to provide school culture and safety staff through May 2023
output.summary: This amendment adds $276,300 to the Saving Shorty contract, raising the limit from $90,000 to $366,300. Saving Shorty will provide up to 13 people and one supervisor for added culture and safety support at schools chosen by the district. Staff build positive relationships with youth, use de-escalation skills and monitor school areas. The service period is January 1 through May 31, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for an evaluator of the district's federal human trafficking prevention grant
output.summary: An individual contractor will evaluate the federal Human Trafficking Youth Prevention Education grant program. The work includes analyzing pre- and post-tests from students and staff, helping with quarterly performance reports, and joining the federal site visit. The service period is July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies $1,350 for SPG Therapy & Education to train Dewey Academy staff on behavior management
output.summary: The Speech Pathology Group, doing business as SPG Therapy & Education, will train Dewey Academy staff in strategies for managing student behavior. The service period is January 4 through April 28, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

vendor.name: The Speech Pathology Group dba SPG Therapy & Education

output.headline: Ratifies up to $70,000 for a contractor to run an arts pilot in expanded learning programs
output.summary: An individual contractor will provide project management, community engagement and coordination for a pilot that brings arts into the district's Expanded Learning (after-school) programs. The Community Schools and Student Services Department manages it. The service period is January 4 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,525 for Oakland Genesis Soccer Club to coach students at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: Oakland Genesis Soccer Club will provide coaches for two 90-minute soccer practices a week plus seven game days for students at Allendale Elementary School. The service period is September 16 through December 9, 2022. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $8,640 for a contractor to use Edulastic assessment software for Linked Learning
output.summary: An individual contractor will use the Edulastic assessment software to run assessments and upload student work to a live online database that gives instant feedback. The High School Linked Learning Department manages it. The service period is January 2 through February 28, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for Norman Peterson & Associate to manage injured workers' return to work
output.summary: Norman Peterson & Associate, Inc. will track injured employees' progress, stay in contact with their doctors and supervisors, and help find temporary modified-duty assignments so they can return to work safely. The work is run through the Risk Management Department for July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023. The Board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $100,000 Warriors Community Foundation grant for the Town Reading Warriors literacy project
output.summary: The district is accepting $100,000 from the Warriors Community Foundation for the Town Reading Warriors Project, which aims to increase literacy support for district students. The Academics and Instruction Department will run it from November 23, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Accepts a $75,000 Warriors Community Foundation grant for a student mental health services pilot
output.summary: The district is accepting $75,000 from the Warriors Community Foundation for a pilot to improve mental health services for Oakland students. The Community Schools and Student Services Department will run it from November 22, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Accepts an $81,000 state grant for Oakland High's Law and Public Service Academy
output.summary: The district is accepting $81,000 from the California Department of Education through the California Partnership Academies career technical education program. The money is for the Law and Public Service Academy at Oakland High School. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts an $81,000 state grant for Skyline High's Computer Science and Technology Academy
output.summary: The district is accepting $81,000 from the California Department of Education through the California Partnership Academies career technical education program. The money is for the Computer Science and Technology Academy at Skyline High School. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts an $81,000 state grant for Oakland Tech's Fashion Academy
output.summary: The district is accepting $81,000 from the California Department of Education through the California Partnership Academies career technical education program. The money is for the Fashion Academy at Oakland Technical High School. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts an $81,000 state grant for Oakland International High's Multimedia Communications Academy
output.summary: The district is accepting $81,000 from the California Department of Education through the California Partnership Academies career technical education program. The money is for the Multimedia Communications Academy at Oakland International High School. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts an $81,000 state grant for Oakland High's Public Health and Policy Academy
output.summary: The district is accepting $81,000 from the California Department of Education through the California Partnership Academies career technical education program. The money is for the Public Health and Policy Academy at Oakland High School. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts an $85,000 Stupski Foundation grant to support anti-bias training for the district
output.summary: The district is accepting $85,000 from the Stupski Foundation to support anti-bias training for the district, as described in the district's grant request dated August 30, 2022. The High School Linked Learning Office will manage it from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $18,500 for Quetzal Education Consulting's anti-racist math training at Oakland Tech

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $18,500.00

output.summary: The board is approving, after the fact, a contract with Quetzal Education Consulting to run a professional development series on anti-racist math for the math teachers at Oakland Technical High School. The work period began January 3, 2023 and runs through June 30, 2023. The district can pay up to $18,500.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,200 for Luna Dance Institute to coach elementary dance teachers

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,200.00

output.summary: The board is approving, after the fact, a contract with Luna Dance Institute of Berkeley to provide coaching and mentoring to elementary dance teachers. The goal is to build up dance teaching in the district. The work period began December 1, 2022 and runs through June 30, 2023, and the district can pay up to $10,200.

output.headline: Accepts a $514,528 California Department of Education grant for career and technical education
output.summary: The board is accepting a grant of $514,528 from the California Department of Education under the Strengthening Career and Technical Education for the 21st Century Act. The money goes to the district's High School Linked Learning Office for the purposes described in the grant attachment. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Revises the job description for the district's Deputy General Counsel for Labor & Employment
output.summary: The Board is adopting Resolution No. 2223-0107, which revises the official job description for the Deputy General Counsel, Labor & Employment, in the Labor Department. The official text does not say what changed in the description.

output.headline: Extends the City of Oakland's lease of a modular library building at Piedmont Elementary
output.summary: The board is approving a first amendment to a joint-use lease that lets the City of Oakland use an existing modular building at Piedmont Elementary School as a public library. The City pays the district $2,500 a month. The lease is extended until the earlier of the completion of the library construction project or five years. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the January 25, 2023 regular Board of Education meeting
output.summary: The board is approving the written record of its regular meeting held on January 25, 2023. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. There is no cost.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the January 25, 2023 special Board of Education meeting
output.summary: The board is approving the written record of its special meeting held on January 25, 2023. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. There is no cost.

output.headline: Ratifies the board president's three appointments to the 2023 Teaching and Learning Committee
output.summary: The board is approving the board president's picks for its standing Teaching and Learning Committee for 2023. VanCedric Williams is chair, and Benjamin “Sam” Davis and Jennifer Brouhard are members. There is no cost.

output.headline: Ratifies the reappointment of two members to the Audit Committee through January 2025
output.summary: The board is approving the board president's reappointment of Elizabeth Ross (third term) and Jason Joseph (second term) to the Audit Committee. The text says each has given satisfactory service so far. The new term runs February 1, 2023 through January 31, 2025.

output.headline: Ratifies the reappointment of three members to the Measure G Committee through January 2025
output.summary: The board is approving the board president's reappointment of Patricia Lee (second term), Harold Lowe (third term) and Stephanie Hawke (second term) to the Measure G Committee. The text says each has given satisfactory service so far. The new term runs February 1, 2023 through January 31, 2025.
